newsitem.title: UK: BADMINTON-HOYER-LARSEN STRUGGLES INTO SECOND ROUND.
newsitem.headline: BADMINTON-HOYER-LARSEN STRUGGLES INTO SECOND ROUND.

text.p: Olympic champion Poul-Erik Hoyer-Larsen produced some late-night drama before advancing to the last 16 of the world championships on Wednesday.
The Danish world number two who set the Olympic gold alongside the European championship and All-England titles in an outstanding 1996 has struggled to reproduce similar form this year.
He gave an unconvincing performance against Malaysian Wong Choon Han before going through 18-16 15-11.
With all his matches having been scheduled in the late evening session, Hoyer-Larsen admitted his preparation had been far from ideal.

"When you finish late, it is difficult to get something to eat and I also have difficulty sleeping," he said. "When you are following other matches it is also difficult to time your build-up. You never know when you are going to be on court."
Hoyer-Larsen admitted he was irritated over always being billed as the night attraction. He was often on court after midnight at the All-England championships in March.
It was the unseeded Wong who set the pace in the opening game. He led 12-10 and 13-12 before an out-of-touch Hoyer-Larsen battled back to 13-13 and went on to take it 18-16.

Wong also led in the early stages of the second game before Hoyer-Larsen drew ahead at 4-3. The Malaysian was always on his heels from then on and it was a relieved second seed who went through to meet number 14 seed Luo Yigang of China.
Chinese top seed Dong Jiong also failed to hit top form but was never in danger of defeat by Russia's Pavel Uvarov. The All-England champion won 15-4 15-5.

In the women's event Ye Zhaoying, the Chinese top seed, took just 11 minutes to defeat Australia's Commonwealth Games champion Lisa Campbell 11-1 11-1 and the 1993 champion, Susi Susanti of Indonesia, was kept on court one minute longer in beating Taiwan's Chan Ya-Lin by the same score.
